clue.text: Gay, operatic relict with mere dowry restored

indicators.note: restored suggests putting things back into a different order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful widow in an opera recovers her dowry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges the thirteen letters of WITH MERE DOWRY. 'Gay' here has its old sense of merry, and a relict is an old word for a widow: Lehár's operetta.
explanation.definitionFit: Lehár's operetta is named for a cheerful widowed heroine, and a relict is a widow.

clue.text: High fashion around Panama?

parts.note: reads like couture in Central America, but describes a strip of ribbon worn round a hat such as a panama

explanation.surface: Smart clothing seen in the Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: Panama is a straw hat as well as a country; what goes round it high up on the head is this ribbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ribbon circling the crown of a hat, here a panama, worn high on the head.

clue.text: Handicapped threesome detailed by bucolic lady?

definitions.text: Handicapped threesome detailed by bucolic lady?

parts.words: Handicapped threesome detailed by bucolic lady?
parts.note: the nursery rhyme trio who were blind and had their tails cut off by the farmer's wife

explanation.surface: A disabled trio described in detail by a countrywoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' means de-tailed: the farmer's wife (the 'bucolic lady') cut off their tails with a carving knife in the rhyme Three Blind Mice.
explanation.definitionFit: The three blind rodents of the nursery rhyme lost their tails to a farmer's wife.

clue.text: Vexing questions for gardeners

explanation.surface: Puzzling problems that trouble keen gardeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzles are posed as brainteasers; gardeners also use coarse soil sieves of that name.

clue.text: Yard sunshade is opening wide

parts.note: an awning is a canvas sunshade over a window or shop

explanation.surface: A garden canopy is being opened out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping like a mouth or chasm that stretches open.

clue.text: Figure represented in mosaic, once

indicators.note: the answer is shown within the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A shape that was once portrayed in a tiled picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented in' points into mosaIC ONce.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious image or symbolic figure, often painted or set in tiles.

clue.text: Oh, super arrangement for the old lutanist

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters, as of music, puts these words in a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a fine musical arrangement of an ancient lute tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' reorders OH SUPER. The surface's musical arrangement suits the mythical player of the lyre.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Greek musician charmed beasts and even the underworld with his lyre playing.

clue.text: Chalet Charles converted to keep in Wales

indicators.note: a building converted is changed in form, so these letters are remade

explanation.surface: A man named Charles has turned his chalet into a Welsh stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges CHALET CHARLES. A keep is the tower of a castle, so 'keep' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval fortress on the Gwynedd coast, built by Edward I.

clue.text: Peevish sort spaniel found in vault

parts.note: peevish means cross, irritable
a springer is a sort of spaniel

explanation.surface: A grumpy dog is discovered in a burial chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vault' is the arched roof of architecture, not a leap or a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An architectural term for a diagonal rib springing up in groined vaulting.

clue.text: Worker with sour taste needs this stomach medicine

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker
an acid flavour is a sour one

explanation.surface: A labourer with a bitter taste in his mouth needs an indigestion remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that neutralises stomach acidity to relieve indigestion.

clue.text: Monstrous lie about women's jumper

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a hopper is something that jumps

explanation.surface: A huge fib told about a woman's sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like the knitted garment, but it is a thing that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a huge falsehood, a barefaced fib.

clue.text: Conduct chosen by Bassanio

explanation.surface: Behaviour picked by a Shakespearean suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Merchant of Venice Bassanio wins Portia by choosing the casket made of the dull metal rather than gold or silver.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide or direct; also the base metal of the casket Bassanio picks.

clue.text: Spain's wettest part — that is evident

explanation.surface: The rainiest region of Spain is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The song from My Fair Lady: the rain in Spain stays mainly on this flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat open land, from the song line about rain in Spain; also clear and obvious.

clue.text: Canal backing up, by Jove!

indicators.note: backing up means going backwards, so the canal's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a waterway's traffic reverses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Jove!' reads as an exclamation; 'by' is the link and Jove the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jove is the Roman name for the king of the gods, Greek counterpart Zeus's equal.

clue.text: Gold sovereign

parts.note: reads as a British gold coin but means a king associated with gold

explanation.surface: An old British gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is a gold coin worth one pound; here it is a king, the Phrygian ruler whose touch turned things to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Phrygian king whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Two points plus four points — put that in record book

parts.note: E (east) is one compass point
N (north) is the other compass point
a try in rugby union was worth four points when this was set

explanation.surface: A scorer adds up a rugby tally and notes it down.
explanation.walkthrough: The two points are compass points, east and north; a rugby try scored four points until 1992 (now five).
explanation.definitionFit: An item written into a register or log is a record.

clue.text: Iron transporters, of course?

parts.note: reads like freight carriers of metal, but means bag carriers who bear golf clubs round a golf course

explanation.surface: Ships carrying iron ore, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means 'of the golf course': golf irons are carried by these attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf attendants carry a player's clubs, irons included, around the links.

clue.text: Here's Book 1, seeing second is damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Bible reader finds the first book's second page torn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges SEEING plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening book of the Bible, telling of creation.

clue.text: Abbe endlessly imprisoned becomes a vegetable

annotationWithheld.why: Abbe endlessly imprisoned becomes a vegetable: ABB inside CAGE, but 'imprisoned' would be both the container indicator and the only word giving CAGE
annotationWithheld.clue: Abbe endlessly imprisoned becomes a vegetable

clue.text: Meteorologists' equipment, blessing to include everybody

indicators.note: one word is made to take in another, which sits inside it

parts.note: a boon is a blessing
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters see their equipment as a godsend for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather forecasters send gas-filled bags aloft to measure the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: I is one; O for another!

definitions.text: I is one; O for another!

parts.words: I is one; O for another!
parts.note: reads like grammar about a letter, but I and O are symbols for iodine and oxygen

explanation.surface: A remark on letters standing for numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: I and O look like the numeral one and a zero; they are the chemical symbols for iodine and oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine and oxygen are chemical substances on the periodic table.

clue.text: Wehster's drawing-room?

parts.note: reads like the dictionary maker's lounge, but a webster is a web-spinner, the spider who invites the fly into this room

explanation.surface: Where the dictionary compiler entertained guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Webster suggests the dictionary; read it as 'web-ster', a spider: 'Will you walk into my parlour?' said the spider to the fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word for a sitting room, as in the poem of the spider and the fly.

clue.text: Mythical mount from which to see the constellation

explanation.surface: From a legendary peak one can view the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests a mountain; it is a steed, the winged horse of Greek myth, also a northern star group.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse ridden by Bellerophon, which also names a group of stars.

clue.text: Top gear, undeniably

parts.note: a garment that is quite literally top gear since it is worn over everything else

explanation.surface: Unquestionably the best clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top gear' sounds like the finest kit; this protective garment is top gear because it goes over all one's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose protective garment worn on top of ordinary clothes.

clue.text: Sunday bowler transferred for profit

annotationWithheld.why: Sunday bowler transferred for profit: S plus OLD is the likely shape, but no reading of 'bowler' gives OLD, and no source gives the parse

clue.text: Row of bushes indicating hospital boundary

parts.note: an edge is a boundary

explanation.surface: A line of shrubs marks where the hospital grounds end.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of closely planted shrubs forming a living fence.

clue.text: Irishman living in Chelsea, normally

indicators.note: the name lives inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An Irish man who usually lives in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'living in' points into chelSEA Normally. Chelsea is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish form of John, a common Irish man's name.

clue.text: This is an eye-opener, love, on the bathing beach

parts.note: an eyelid is what opens the eye
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A revelation for a sweetheart at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opener' looks like a surprise; it is the eyelid, which opens over the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A public open-air pool or beach resort for swimming.

clue.text: Such an atmosphere when: painter is crowned with gold

indicators.note: in a down entry the crown is the top, so one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: An artist wearing a golden crown has a special glow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the crown is the top, so 'is crowned with' sets the gold above the painter; 'when:' is padding in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive air or glow surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: See sights depicted in oils by East

indicators.note: depicted means painted in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist sees the sights painted in oils by an Eastern artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicted' rearranges the letters of the two words before it, giving LIONIS, and East follows. 'See sights' is the old verb sense, as of a visitor touring a city's attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the verb: to visit the notable attractions of a place.

clue.text: Banger. South American custom-built

parts.note: usage is custom or habit

explanation.surface: A loud explosive, specially made in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGER is British slang for a sausage, not a firework or old car here.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a meat link, from its habit of bursting when fried.

clue.text: Since no battle manoeuvres, there can be no dispute

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres are moved about, so these letters shift position

explanation.surface: With no fighting taking place, the matter is settled beyond argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges SINCE NO BATTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond question or argument; impossible to challenge.
